item.title: Strain-enabled dynamical magnetoelectric coupling in BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical excitation has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating and creating non-equilibrium phases of matter. Yet, the pathways available for optical control are intrinsically limited by the symmetries and interactions of the equilibrium system. Here, we demonstrate that these pathways can be redesigned through atomic-structural engineering to access hidden dynamical properties. By combining resonant vibrational excitation with epitaxial strain, we realize a light-induced, room-temperature multiferroic state in strained thin films of the technologically relevant hexagonal ferrimagnet, barium hexaferrite (BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$, BaM). Time-resolved second harmonic generation and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements reveal an enhanced ferroelectric polarization together with a weakening of the magnetic moment upon exciting mid-infrared phonons in strained BaM thin films, but not in the bulk material. Structural analysis and first-principles-based theory show that this effect is enabled by strain-generated displacement of Fe$^{3+}$ ions, which break the local symmetry and facilitate an emergent dynamical magnetoelectric coupling. Both the strong lattice excitation and strain-induced symmetry breaking are essential for enabling this dynamical coupling, promising an important template for designing otherwise inaccessible non-equilibrium phenomena.

item.title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.31503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute conductivity--shear-modulus cross-property bounds in three-dimensional isotropic two-phase composites using the translation method, and obtain the tightest bounds reported to date. To assess attainability, we perform unit-cell topology optimization on thousands of distinct initial structures and compare optimized designs to the isotropic bounds using an effective-medium approximation that models the macroscopic material as an isotropic assembly of randomly oriented grains. The best jointly performing designs are consistently bicontinuous, triply periodic minimal surface-like microstructures; however, a small but notable gap to the translation bound remains.

item.title: Electrical Degradation of Vertical $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Au-Ion Irradiation to a Fluence of $1.3 \times 10^7$ cm$^{-2}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

item.title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in $\gamma$-InSe
item.description: arXiv:2611.31537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in $\gamma$-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of $3.8\times10^{-6}~\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in $\gamma$-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.

item.title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.31672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range $4 \le \text{pH} \le 14$ under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range ($0 \le \text{pH} \le 14$). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40\%, well above the 10\% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68\% under a tensile strain of +6\%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.

item.title: Magic-layer scenario for predicting non-van der Waals two-dimensional materials: The case of double-layer honeycomb structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.31748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A magic number is a specific size of a van der Waals (vdW) cluster that shows pronounced stability compared to adjacent sizes, and therefore magic clusters are preferentially formed in experiments. We apply the ``magic-layer'' concept to identify non-vdW two-dimensional (2D) materials that are difficult to exfoliate from their parent 3D crystals. As a case, we study the stability of thin films in III-V, II-VI, I-VII, and Mn-based compounds using first-principles calculations. By calculating excess energies for various thicknesses, we find significant stabilization reflecting the formation of double-layer honeycomb structures at specific thicknesses. The stability measure based on the magic-layer concept can distinguish the experimentally synthesized systems from the experimentally unrealized systems, which serves as a key descriptor for predicting the realization of non-vdW 2D materials.
item.dc:creator: Shota Ono

item.title: Accelerating Equivariant Interatomic Potentials for Molecular Dynamics through Radial tabulation and Kernel Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.31865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) achieve near-quantum-chemical accuracy, but their computational cost and GPU memory footprint restrict molecular dynamics (MD) at extended length and time scales. Even when the tensor product (TP) is accelerated, both bottlenecks remain governed by evaluating and storing per-edge radial weights in the NequIP convolution. We introduce JET-MLIPs (Joint-Kernel Equivariant Convolution with Tabulated Radial Weights for MLIP simulation), a GPU backend applicable to pretrained NequIP-family potentials without retraining. JET-MLIPs replaces the radial multilayer perceptron (MLP) with a piecewise cubic Hermite table and fuses table lookup, spherical harmonics, TP and neighbor aggregation into a single kernel, eliminating per-edge radial-weight and MLP-intermediate storage during force evaluation. Across 15 released potentials from SevenNet, MACE, NequIP-OAM, Nequix and EquFlash on a 5632-atom liquid electrolyte, LAMMPS MD attains 1.5-5.9$\times$ step-time speed-ups and 2.4-24$\times$ peak memory reductions relative to each family's existing TP-accelerated backend on a single H200 GPU while preserving single-precision (fp32) accuracy and dynamical stability. These reductions enable multi-nanosecond transport-property simulations of roughly $10^4$-atom systems on a single GPU and broaden access to large-scale equivariant MLIP MD on widely available GPUs.
item.dc:creator: Jaekyun Yoo, Suyeon Ju

item.title: From Weighted Frontier d-States to Geometric Descriptors for Atomically Dispersed Catalysts at the Molecule-Solid Crossover
item.description: arXiv:2611.32059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomically dispersed catalysts exhibit molecule-solid crossover character when localized metal orbitals hybridize with support-derived bands, a regime not fully captured by either a d-band-center description or a frontier-orbital picture. We establish an electronic-to-geometric framework for oxygen reduction across fourteen metals. N-to-P substitution in M-N4 sites raises theoretical onset potentials in 13 systems, with Rh-N3P reaching 0.88 V, comparable to the Pt(111) benchmark. Scaling relations reduce *OOH, *O, and *OH thermodynamics to $\Delta$G*OH. M-N4 follows a dyz-dominated frontier-orbital picture, whereas M-N3P requires a weighted frontier d-state representation built from adsorption-relevant orbitals and their occupancies. The resulting $\epsilon$WFDS correlates with $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.92, compared with 0.83 for the d-band center and 0.64 for the frontier-orbital. The identified roles of orbital occupancy and local coordination suggest an interpretable geometric descriptor, $\zeta$M-N3P = nd/rM-P, that predicts $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.96. The ORR volcano analysis identifies strong-binding systems and motivates axial oxygen coordination. This design raises onset potentials by 0.70-2.46 V, and the M-N3PO descriptor predicts $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.91. By bridging frontier-orbital and d-band-center descriptions, the framework provides a physically grounded electronic representation and a geometry-based screening route compatible with machine-learned interatomic potentials.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Li, Zewen Wu, Longling Pang, Zhidan Li, Xianghua Kong

item.title: Emergent Electric-Field-Tunable $p$-Wave Magnetism in Twisted Bilayer NiPS$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.32103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A perpendicular electric field can reorient a momentum-space spin texture without changing the local magnetic configuration. In this Letter, we investigate this mechanism in a $21^\circ$-twisted $\mathrm{NiPS}_3$ bilayer with zigzag order and coplanar, nonparallel layer N\'eel vectors. In the ideal nonrelativistic limit, an antiunitary in-plane half-translation enforces opposite-spin pairing at opposite momenta, while a layer-exchanging twofold operation pins the leading $p$-wave spin splitting to a crystallographic direction. A perpendicular layer bias lifts this orientational constraint while preserving the antiunitary symmetry, allowing a transverse component of the splitting vector. First-principles calculations show gate-dependent reorientation and deformation of spin-resolved isoenergy contours. Wannier-based linear-response calculations further reveal field-activated diagonal spin conductivities and a polarity-dependent tilt in the angular profile of the transverse spin-current response. The spin-texture axis, dispersion axes, and transport-response axis are distinct quantities governed by the same symmetry reduction. These results identify layer bias as a route to controlling odd-parity spin textures and spin-current anisotropy, provided that the coplanar magnetic state remains stable.
item.dc:creator: Jiaran Su, Jin-Xin Hu, Qi Sun, Dante M. Kennes, Yuhao Fu, Lede Xian, Lijun Zhang

item.title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.32370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.
item.dc:creator: Miguel A. L. Marques, Irene D'Amico, Stefano Pittalis

item.title: Continuum model for disconnection structures of hetero-interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.32412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hetero-interfaces, as planar defects between dissimilar materials, accommodate the lattice misfit through networks of line defects of disconnections (a combination of structural ledges/step and dislocation characters). We develop a continuum model that predicts the hetero-interface structures, including disconnection networks, the interface inclination and misorientation angles. The model is based on the interfacial energy minimization with respect to all possible disconnection modes, subject to the interface structure constraint of the generalized Frank-Bilby equation that describes the lattice correspondence across the interface including both dislocation and step characters of disconnections and the inclination and misorientation angles. Numerical simulations are performed to determine the equilibrium configurations of three different types of hetero-interfaces: the $\alpha$/$\beta$ (orthorhombic/monoclinic) interface in ZrO$_2$, $\alpha$/$\beta$ hetero-interfaces in Ti and Au/Pd (001) twist-misfit interfaces. Comparisons with experiments, atomistic simulations and theoretical predictions show that our continuum model provides excellent predictions of the hetero-interface structures including disconnection networks and inclination, misorientation angles. Furthermore, systematic analysis reveals the functional dependence of hetero-interface structural properties on inclination and misorientation angles.
item.dc:creator: Luchan Zhang, Xiaoxue Qin, Dongsong Tao, Jian Han, David J. Srolovitz, Yang Xiang

item.title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
item.description: arXiv:2611.32609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.
item.dc:creator: Raynol Dsouza, Thomas D. Swinburne, J\"org Neugebauer

item.title: Spin-Group versus Magnetic-Group Selection Rules for Nonlinear Photocurrents in Compensated Ferrimagnets
item.description: arXiv:2611.32618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical excitation offers a contact-free, ultrafast route to charge and spin currents, with symmetry determining which nonlinear photocurrents are allowed and whether they carry charge, spin, or both. Spin-group symmetry describes the limit without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), whereas magnetic-group symmetry accounts for SOC. We show that the two descriptions yield different selection rules for both charge and spin photocurrents in the multiferroic compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO$_3$. Without SOC, only linear shift and circular injection currents are allowed, with identical components for charge and spin, so every charge current is spin polarized along the moments. SOC leaves these charge currents nearly unchanged, activates magnetic linear injection and circular shift charge currents, and enables pure spin currents polarized perpendicular to the moments. Ferroelectric switching reverses the linear shift and circular injection charge currents and their spin polarization. These findings establish the importance of magnetic-group symmetry for a complete description of nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnets.
item.dc:creator: Fu Li, Vikrant Chaudhary, Weiyi Pan, Hongbin Zhang, Harish K. Singh

item.title: Constrained Allen-Cahn phase-field topology optimization of flexoelectric devices
item.description: arXiv:2611.32620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization provides an effective approach to exploring performance-oriented designs for miniature devices. In this work, a phase-field framework for constrained topology optimization of microscale flexoelectric devices is developed using a continuum model under the assumption of infinitesimal deformations. The material distribution is optimized at the device level with the output voltage as the objective. The framework also accommodates objectives based on capacitance or stored electrostatic energy. Manufacturing variations are incorporated through a worst-case objective over the prescribed geometric realizations, with spectral constraints imposed to maintain the structural connectivity. The framework is applied to two-dimensional pressure and bending sensors and a three-dimensional thin-film device. The optimized nominal output voltages reach approximately 4.8 times the initial value for the pressure sensor and 2.5-3.4 times the initial values for the bending sensors. The voltage gains arise primarily from increased mechanically induced source charge, with capacitance reduction providing an additional contribution that varies with the device configuration. Erosion analyses of representative designs further show that structural connectivity is well preserved when structural members become locally narrower, with the output voltage remaining close to that of the nominal configuration. Combined with specific microfabrication processes, this optimization framework is expected to provide a numerical basis for configuration screening and prototype development of flexoelectric devices.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhen, Sheng Mao

item.title: Comparative Molecular Dynamics Study of Initial Oxide Film Growth on Al, Mg, and Ti Using a Universal Neural Network Potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.32659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spontaneous formation of an oxide film, which may be passive, is found in many metals such as Al and Ti. We report direct computational observation of oxide film formation on the three major light structural metals, Al, Mg, and Ti, with molecular dynamics (MD) using a universal neural network potential (NNP). O2 molecules were supplied during MD simulations to replenish O consumed by the metal. Al and Ti formed a 1-2 nm thick film within a few ps of the simulation with O2 gas pressure of 102-103 atm. The film thicknesses of all metal oxides continued to increase proportionally to the logarithm of simulation time, consistent with Cabrera-Mott theory. Al and Ti oxides grow at the surface, while Mg oxide grows into the Mg metal. Al, Mg, and Ti are approximately 4.4, 4.3, and 5.2-fold coordinated, respectively, in the oxide.
item.dc:creator: Yoyo Hinuma, Taisuke Hasegawa

item.title: A macroscopic-atom spectral theory of grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys
item.description: arXiv:2611.32701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys remains challenging because existing spectral approaches require alloy-specific atomistic calculations to resolve segregation-energy distributions and correlations across non-equivalent boundary sites. Here, we develop a transferable macroscopic-atom spectral theory that predicts the joint segregation behavior of multiple species from physically interpretable elemental descriptors. The theory is founded on the finding that local strain and bond deficit account for 91\% of the site-to-site co-variation of 40 solutes in a density-functional-theory (DFT) Al polycrystal. Linked to atomic size and surface enthalpy, these coordinates allow prediction of individual segregation spectra and their cross-species correlations, which determine whether species compete for or share grain-boundary sites. A closed-system formulation unifies host-element redistribution and dilute-solute segregation, couples metallic and light-element sublattices, and accounts for bulk compound formation and solute pairing. Calibrated using binary spectra only, the theory predicts unseen-host spectral means with a correlation coefficient of 0.81, outperforms embedded-atom spectra against DFT benchmarks, and ranks site competition across 870 solute pairs with a Spearman coefficient of 0.90. Without fitting to multicomponent observations, it reproduces 11 of 12 equilibrium Fe ternaries and 49 of 55 Mg ternaries. Predictions recorded before simulations of an 82,699-atom polycrystal identify site competition as the baseline behavior and metal-metalloid pair chemistry as a source of deviations requiring atomistic resolution. These results establish a physically grounded route to screening grain-boundary chemistry in multicomponent alloys, including steels and high-entropy alloys.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Boakye, Chuang Deng

item.title: Reversible Self-Assembly of a P-Ir(100)-P Trilayer on Ir(111)
item.description: arXiv:2611.32706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adsorbate-induced surface reconstructions offer a route to engineer low-dimensional materials with atomic arrangements and electronic properties fundamentally different from those of their parent substrates. Here, we demonstrate how phosphorus adsorption on Ir(111) drives the formation of an incommensurate P-Ir-P trilayer, in which a square Ir(100)-like atomic lattice emerges from the underlying hexagonal crystal. This transformation illustrates how strong adsorbate-substrate interactions can stabilize unconventional atomic coordination within an ultrathin metallic structure. Remarkably, the process is reversible, allowing the system to switch between distinct structural phases through phosphorus deposition and thermal annealing. The resulting trilayer exhibits a two-dimensional, semimetal-like electronic structure dominated by Ir 5d states. Our findings establish adsorbate-driven symmetry transformation as a strategy for engineering atomically thin transition-metal compounds with structural and electronic properties inaccessible through conventional surface growth.
item.dc:creator: M. Bassotti, J. Sivianes, J. Dai, M. Tallarida, P. Angulo-Portugal, A. A. Makarova, J. Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, D. Yu. Usachov, A. Verdini, F. Schiller

item.title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.32723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling. Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.
item.dc:creator: Anastasiia Nihei, Rico Friedrich

item.title: Neutron Spectroscopy Transformed: Deuterated ZIF-8 and Machine-Learned Potentials Catch Nitrogen Threading Its Gates
item.description: arXiv:2611.32739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a step change in what inelastic neutron scattering (INS) can reveal, by combining machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with deliberate deuteration of the sample. INS's prowess in charting framework and guest motions within porous materials during in situ dosing has historically had one caveat: costly density-functional-theory calculations are a major bottleneck in the speed and depth of analysis. We show that rapid frontier MLIPs remove this bottleneck on both counts, keeping pace with the experiment while bringing a new level of insight. Deuterating the linkers of ZIF-8 pries apart bands that overlap in the hydrogenous framework, and we test four MLIPs against eight stages of nitrogen dosing at 77 K. On loading, a previously unobserved band appears at 270 cm^-1 and grows gradually through the dosing series. The simulations trace it to single N2 molecules threaded end-on through four-ring windows, each turning its ring of linkers and propping the window open, and unbiased dynamics catch molecules threading into the windows on their own, finding a free-energy trap that crowding stabilizes. This is the first vibrational signature of the threaded state and, crucially, its intensity directly counts the threading over the slow, macroscopic timescale of gas uptake, in situ. More broadly, the simulations explain how each framework band responds to its guests, establishing MLIP-assisted inelastic neutron scattering as a route to mechanism, not just assignment.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, Matthew E. Potter

item.title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.32761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heat flow across the core-mantle boundary (CMB) depends on the lattice thermal conductivity ($\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$) of lowermost-mantle minerals, yet calculated CMB values for MgO differ severalfold, and high-temperature estimates of the conductivity increase across the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition range from about 20 to 50%. Direct solutions of the linearized phonon Boltzmann transport equation (LBTE) require thousands of density functional theory (DFT) force evaluations per thermodynamic state. Here we replace these evaluations with phase-specific, fine-tuned MACE potentials for MgO, MgSiO3 bridgmanite (Pv), and MgSiO3 post-perovskite (PPv). The potentials reproduce DFT energies, forces, stresses, pressure-volume relations, and compressed-state phonons for all three phases. For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes $\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$ by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K. PPv is 44-55% more conductive than Pv at the same pressure and temperature and strongly anisotropic, with $\kappa_{[100]}/\kappa_{[010]}$ ranging from 1.7 to 2.1. The quasi-harmonic phase boundary has a Clapeyron slope of $(7.4 \pm 0.1)$ MPa/K and intersects a model geotherm at 116.2 GPa and 2660 K, where the transition raises the silicate conductivity by 47%, to 8.6 W/(m K). Heating in the basal thermal boundary layer lowers the MgO and PPv conductivities to 37.3 and 6.7 W/(m K) at the CMB, where Hashin-Shtrikman bounds of 9.5-11.4 W/(m K) for an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO encompass the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates. The density-temperature parameterizations provide an intrinsic end-member reference for lower-mantle thermal models.
item.dc:creator: Amrendra Kumar Tiwari, Sandro Jahn

item.title: Nanoparticles with a BANG: Detonation-Driven Synthesis of Metals and Metal Oxides
item.description: arXiv:2611.32985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bristol Accelerated Nanoparticle Generation (BANG) method is a solvent- and capping-agent-free nanoparticle synthesis. Previous work was limited mostly to gold, silver and copper particles. Here, the method is extended to ten further elements, including Pb, Bi, Tl, Mn, Fe, Zn, Pt, Ni, Cd and Pd. Detonation in air favoured metal formation for less oxophilic metals, whereas detonation of silver azide under nitrogen suppressed detectable silver oxide formation while retaining locally identified hexagonal close-packed (HCP) Ag alongside face-centred cubic (FCC) Ag. The outcome of the synthesis can be modified by changing the detonation environment, while the highly non-equilibrium conditions provide access to phases that are difficult to obtain using conventional synthetic routes. BANG is a broadly applicable, highly non-equilibrium nanoparticle synthesis method whose products are governed by precursor chemistry and atmosphere, with potential access to kinetically trapped phases and direct supported-particle deposition.
item.dc:creator: Jan Maurycy Uszko, Robert Maty\'a\v{s}, Naoto Shirahata, Stephen J. Eichhorn, Avinash J. Patil, Simon R. Hall

item.title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.33060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Native vacancy populations in transition-metal nitride coatings reflect vacancy formation, association, and depth-dependent stability. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compare these effects in rocksalt TiN and CrN in bulk and at (001) surfaces, within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges. In TiN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ is favoured under N-poor and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ under N-rich conditions; in CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ remains preferred throughout its stability range. Association energies are referenced to corresponding isolated vacancies where positive values mean association lowers the energy and negative values favour separation. Mean bulk association energies for mixed metal-nitrogen pairs are $+0.132$ eV in TiN and $+1.053$ eV in CrN. At (001) surfaces, $V_\mathrm{N}$ in TiN prefers the surface and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ the first subsurface layer. In CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ has similar formation energies at the surface and first subsurface layer, with a slight preference for the latter; $V_\mathrm{Cr}$ slightly prefers the second subsurface layer. Surface cluster energies are referenced to separated vacancies at their preferred depths. The compact $2V_\mathrm{Ti}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ cluster in TiN has favourable association in bulk ($+0.217$ eV per vacancy) but unfavourable association at the surface ($-0.346$ eV per vacancy). By contrast, $2V_\mathrm{Cr}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ in CrN remains stabilised, with its association energy decreasing from $+1.188$ to $+0.431$ eV per vacancy. CrN's stronger association occurs without larger structural distortions and is accompanied by distinct Cr-centred magnetic responses.

item.title: Anharmonic enhancement of thermal conductivity in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$: A consistent picture from molecular dynamics and Wigner transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.33089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anharmonicity limits heat conduction in crystals, but its role in amorphous solids, where heat is carried mainly by tunneling between quasi-degenerate vibrations, remains unsettled. Here we disentangle the contributions of structural disorder, quantum statistics, and anharmonicity to the thermal conductivity of amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (aGST), the prototypical phase-change memory material. Using a single machine-learned potential trained on first-principles data, we compare classical equilibrium and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (MD), which include anharmonicity to all orders, with harmonic Allen-Feldman theory and the anharmonic Wigner transport equation, both of which include quantum statistics. Four MD approaches agree on a conductivity of 0.171-0.181 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, about 16% above the harmonic Allen-Feldman value for the same model, and the Wigner formulation bridges the two: with classical statistics, it agrees with MD to within 5%. We trace this anharmonic enhancement to vibrational couplings that grow with the frequency difference between modes, so that anharmonic broadening opens additional channels for heat conduction. A comparison with silica, alumina, and disordered carbons reveals three regimes, in which anharmonicity reduces, barely affects, or enhances the conductivity. The predicted glass-like increase of the conductivity with temperature is consistent with thermoreflectance measurements. These results show that anharmonicity has no universal effect in disordered solids, and can promote rather than limit heat transport in strongly disordered materials.

item.title: Compositionally Tunable Synthesis of High-Entropy Transition Metal Dichalcogenides Exhibiting Above-Room-Temperature Magnetism
item.description: arXiv:2611.33115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As silicon-based electronics approach their physical limits, low-dimensional magnetic materials have attracted increasing attention for next-generation electronic and information technologies. Realizing these opportunities requires two-dimensional (2D) materials with robust and tunable room-temperature magnetism. Here, we report a two-step synthesis strategy for fabricating 2D high-entropy transition metal dichalcogenides (HE-TMDs) incorporating magnetic elements beyond conventional groups 4-6. High-entropy layered double hydroxides (HE-LDHs) are first synthesized via hydrothermal coprecipitation, enabling atomic-level mixing of diverse transition metals across groups 4-12. Subsequent chalcogenization yields 2D HE-TMDs while preserving homogeneous elemental distribution. This approach circumvents the constraints of solid-state reaction, chemical vapor transport methods, enabling the synthesis of compositionally complex and structurally controlled 2D magnets. Representative (VCrFeCoNi)S2-x exhibits robust magnetism above room temperature, demonstrating the potential of this high-entropy design strategy for expanding the compositional and functional diversity of 2D magnetic materials.

item.title: Antiferromagnetic phase of MnTe2: spin-order-induced renormalization of phonon Raman spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2611.33156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, two modes of spin wave excitations (magnons) were detected in Raman scattering spectra of MnTe2. It is an unconventional magnet that features a pyrite-type crystal structure hosting a non-collinear, non-coplanar antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin order below the N\'eel temperature. In this brief communication, the focus is primarily on the effect of spin ordering on lattice dynamics (phonons) that has been established through temperature (5 - 300 K), linear polarization angle (0 deg - 360 deg) and external magnetic field (up to 16 T) dependent measurements. It has been found that below the magnetic transition temperature, the frequencies of four out of five Raman-active lattice vibrations (i.e., Eg and three Tg phonon modes) revealed significant departure from the mechanism of the three-phonon anharmonic decay described by Klemens model. Here, we propose a new model considering spin-phonon coupling to explain frequency renormalization of the phonon part of the Raman spectrum upon the para-/antiferro- (PM/AFM) magnetic phase transition change in MnTe2. Through employing Green's function formalism, we show that a simple two-sublattice collinear antiferromagnet approach follows well both spin ordering induced hardening and softening of phonon modes observed in AFM phase of MnTe2 upon cooling. Additionally, the detailed temperature and field dependences of the energy for both magnon modes are presented. In addition to unexpected twofold anisotropy of the higher energy magnon mode (approx. 3.5 meV) unveiled in crossed configuration, our magneto-optical measurements revealed a subtle, yet definite softening trend for the lower energy mode (approx. 2.6 meV). Although the precise reasons for these effects remain unclear, we put forward a symmetry reduction in the local atomic surroundings as a possible mechanism for discussion.

item.title: Reliability of Language-Model Judges for Quantitative Scientific Question Answering: Evidence from Perovskite Photovoltaics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented language models increasingly relies on automated model judges, yet their reliability on quantitative scientific synthesis remains largely unmeasured. Here, we evaluate automated grading on a quantitative benchmark for perovskite photovoltaics, where all 755 ground-truth answers are deterministically computed from 45,441 experimental device records. We evaluate a frontier judge (Claude Opus 5.5) alongside two local open-weight judges (Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-8B) across 4,530 free-text answers from six retrieval architectures under three regimes: reference-augmented (with the computed key), evidence-augmented (with retrieved passages and query logs), and unassisted (question and answer alone). Equipped with the reference key, Claude Opus reproduces ground truth near-perfectly (Cohen's $\kappa = 0.982 \pm 0.003$) and preserves exact architectural rankings ($\tau = 1.00$). Withholding the reference causes evaluation fidelity to collapse: frontier agreement drops to $\kappa = 0.557 \pm 0.022$, and providing retrieved literature passages yields virtually no improvement ($\kappa = 0.576 \pm 0.024$). Without reference keys, local judges degrade to near-random agreement ($\kappa = 0.087$ and $0.112$), inverting the leaderboard to rank a hallucinating closed-book baseline first ($\tau \le 0.20$). Furthermore, SQL-augmented generations induce severe evaluative blind spots: absent a reference, the frontier judge accepts 46.6% of erroneous SQL answers, overestimating architecture accuracy as 66.4% against its true 52.6%. These findings demonstrate that model-based evaluation in the physical sciences cannot rely on unstructured text inspection; rigorous benchmarking requires reference ground truth precomputed from structured measurement records.

item.title: Self-gravitating dust clumps: linear theory sets the threshold, the onset time and the spacing of their formation, then slow coarsening erases this pattern
item.description: arXiv:2611.31327v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Planets form in disks of gas and dust. One step of their formation is the gathering of dust grains into dense clumps, under their own gravity. This work tries to predict when these clumps appear and how far apart they are. The grains attract each other through a gravity of finite range. The gas slows them down, and its turbulence spreads them out. The grains also cannot go beyond maximum packing: this is volume filling. The dimensionless model depends on two numbers. The first one is the gravitational number $\chi$, which compares attraction with turbulent spreading. The second one is the mean volume fraction $\rho_b$, which measures the amount of grains. We solve the model with second-order finite volumes on an adaptive Cartesian mesh. We then treat each field as an image. An Otsu threshold and a watershed transform isolate the clumps. The code conserves mass to within $10^{-15}$ and converges at second order. Two designs of experiments give 192 simulations in total, with $2\le\chi\le40$ and $0.05\le\rho_b\le0.7$. Linear stability theory predicts the start of clump formation. The instability starts at time $t_{on}\simeq3.0/\sigma^*$, where $\sigma^*$ is the growth rate of the most amplified mode. The dominant wavelength equals the most amplified wavelength to within $10\%$. The area fraction of the clumps equals $\rho_b$. The clumps then go through slow coarsening. A sensitivity analysis attributes most of the variance to $\chi$. The adaptive mesh reduces the computational cost only a little, because the clumps fill the whole domain.

item.title: Origin of quadrupolar order in the 5d$^1$ double perovskite Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite extensive experimental and theoretical studies of quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$, the microscopic origin and relative energy scales of the interactions driving it remain unresolved. In particular, the observed ferroic ordering of the $z^2$ quadrupole has remained difficult to explain, as the relative contributions of superexchange, classical quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, vibronic couplings, and virtual excitations to higher-energy levels have not been established quantitatively. Here, we determine all these interactions from first principles and solve the resulting microscopic Hamiltonian. The calculated ground state reproduces the experimentally observed quadrupolar order parameters and the associated structural distortions with quantitative accuracy. Disentangling the individual contributions, we find that ferroic $z^2$ order originates from a linear-quartic coupling, generated by virtual excitations to the $J_{\mathrm{eff}}$= 1/2 doublet and driven by vibronic interactions. Our results establish the hierarchy of microscopic interactions underlying quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and provide a unified $ab \ initio$ description of its coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.

item.title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and N\'eel temperature
item.description: arXiv:2611.31504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the N\'eel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.

item.title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
item.description: arXiv:2611.31631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.

item.title: Interface and film engineering for improved spin-charge interconversion in sputtered GeTe nanodevices
item.description: arXiv:2611.31816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spin-logic devices promise non-volatile logic-in-memory computing with ultra-low power consumption, offering a route to circumvent the von Neumann bottleneck. Magnetoelectric and ferroelectric spin-orbit (MESO/FESO) devices, however, require spin-charge interconversion materials that combine a large output signal with properties that survive nanoscale integration. Tellurides are particularly fragile in this respect, as processing readily introduces defects that degrade their spin-charge interconversion properties. Here we demonstrate room-temperature spin-charge interconversion in patterned FESO nanoscale devices based on sputtered GeTe, with feature sizes down to 100 nm. By introducing a Ti interfacial layer between the CoFe electrode and GeTe, and by using GeTe films of improved crystalline quality, we increase the interconversion output signal from 3 m{\Omega} to 24 m{\Omega}, exceeding values reported for platinum at comparable device size. These results establish large-scale-deposited GeTe as a viable material platform for spin-logic devices and identify interface quality and film crystallinity as key levers for optimizing their performance.

item.title: Antiferroelectric Fluids with Hierarchical Polar Organization
item.description: arXiv:2611.31959v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The discovery of the ferroelectric nematic (NF) phase has accelerated research on fluids exhibiting polar order along the molecular long axis. However, their antiferroelectric (AFE) counterparts remain less explored. Here, we investigate how terminal alkyl-chain elongation competes with polar core-core interactions in a homologous series. This series exhibits modulated AFE order accompanied by SmC-type cybotactic correlations, with the AFE phase persisting in homologs bearing terminal alkyl chains of up to 17 carbon atoms. Three distinct phase sequences on cooling lead to two types of two-dimensional (2D) AFE lattices. Multiple sharp X-ray diffraction (XRD) peaks reveal rectangular and oblique lattice structures, supporting their classification as AFE columnar phases. XRD analysis and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support a hierarchical structural model in which locally aligned polar molecules occupy thin segments of finite width within polar columns. The columns occupy the sites of a 2D lattice, with neighboring columns polarized in opposite directions. This model provides a structural framework for understanding the distinct precursor phase sequences and links packing between columns to the resulting AFE superstructures.

item.title: Emission regimes and characteristic energy scales in reverse-biased 4H-SiC Schottky barriers: unified field-emission formulas and energy-dependent tunneling effective mass
item.description: arXiv:2611.32146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reverse leakage in 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes is analyzed using a current integral with Fermi-Dirac supply and WKB transmission. The ratio of the interface field to a critical field $F_c$ sets the depth of the thermionic-field-emission (TFE) saddle point. The Airy energy distinguishes the thermionic-tunneling crossover, the validity of the TFE formula, and the TFE/field-emission (FE) boundary, which generalizes to $c_1 k_B T \approx 1$ for arbitrary barrier shapes. Closed-form FE and TFE expressions are given for triangular and quadratic barriers; for the latter, the Padovani-Stratton formulas give 1.4-7.9 times (FE, $10^{19}$ cm$^{-3}$) and 2.5-3.6 times (TFE, low-doped layers, 300-433 K) the WKB current, whereas the present expressions agree within 15% and 2%. Applied to Ti/4H-SiC data (30-160 {\deg}C, 50-950 V), an energy-dependent tunneling mass from the complex band structure reduces the residual from 0.17 to 0.11-0.12 dex; it can be implemented in device simulation via the Franz two-band dispersion.

item.title: Symmetry-dependent field-induced elastic renormalization in the quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy NiCoCr$_{0.8}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.32254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the elastic response of cubic NiCoCr$_{0.8}$, a quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy, by high-precision ultrasound velocity measurements. At zero magnetic field, the three symmetrically independent elastic moduli $C_{11}$, $(C_{11}-C_{12})/2=C_t$, and $C_{44}$ monotonically harden upon cooling without pronounced elastic softening or anomalies. In magnetic fields applied along [110], however, a minute but systematic elastic renormalization of the order of $10^{-5}$ is resolved at low temperatures. The tetragonal $E_g$ mode $C_t$ softens with increasing field, whereas the derived bulk $A_{1g}$ mode $C_B$ hardens, revealing an opposite field response between the two strain-symmetry channels. Comparison with the previously reported quantum-critical-Fermi-liquid crossover scale shows that the field-induced elastic renormalization develops already in the quantum-critical regime and evolves continuously across the crossover region, without a sharp elastic anomaly or threshold behavior. These results demonstrate that symmetry-resolved ultrasound provides a sensitive probe of subtle strain-dependent changes in the electronic and magnetic free energy of a chemically disordered itinerant quantum-critical metal.
item.dc:creator: Tadataka Watanabe, Mai Watanabe, Brian C. Sales

item.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.32265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). The 1T-derived structures remain metallic and magnetic throughout, with $U$ acting mainly as a spectral renormalization. The 1H phase behaves differently, passing from a non-magnetic semiconductor through an antiferromagnetic semiconducting regime before metallizing, so that the gap closes as $U$ increases while the local Cr moment grows monotonically. Biaxial tensile strain at fixed $U$ induces a similar sequence of transitions. Along both tuning pathways, the two inequivalent nearest-neighbor Cr--Cr exchange channels progressively separate and cross, with the parallel-spin channel becoming dominant, accompanied by a breathing-type bond disproportionation. Independent calculations with a localized-orbital implementation reproduce the overall evolution but yield shifted critical values of $U$ and of strain, demonstrating the robustness of the phase diagram while highlighting the implementation dependence of the transition thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Rashmi Ranjan Routaray, Ali Ghojavand, Eric Bousquet

item.title: Periodic and quasiperiodic structures produced by microphase separation in one-component simple liquids with competing interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32273v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Competing interactions can generate frustration which suppresses macroscopic-scale phase separation, superseding it with separation patterns on the microscopic scale. This phenomenon, referred to as microphase separation, produces thermodynamically stable mesoscopic-scale periodic patterns in systems of different physical nature. The studies of this effect follow two paradigms. First, in block copolymers, the macroscopic-scale separation of chemically distinct components is prevented by the covalent bonds between them. In the other, the microscopic-scale separation is produced in simple single-component liquids by the competition between a short-range attraction and a long-range repulsion (SALR) in the pair potential, the separation occurring between a dense phase and a gas. The interest in the simple liquid models with SALR interaction was inspired by the apparent universality of the modulated structures generated by competing interactions in different systems. Simple particle models are tractable by theory and thereby make it possible to discern the microscopic mechanisms of pattern formation; particle-based simulations give access to systems beyond the reach of experiments. In this Perspective we review the recent advances in the molecular-dynamics simulation of microphase separation in single-component simple liquids using SALR potentials. We show that these simulations reproduce the mesophases typical of block copolymers and liquid crystals, which demonstrates that the complexity of the constituent particles of real liquids is not a necessary condition for their formation, and that they produce novel periodic morphologies of both conceptual interest and technological relevance; we discuss how simulated mesophases can serve as templates for metamaterials whose properties are governed by topology.

item.title: Covalent Welding of Two-Dimensional Molecular Sheets into Ultra-Stiff, Super-Tough Polymeric Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.32291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since the inception of macromolecular science, polymers have been constructed from zero-dimensional monomers, a paradigm that funnels all stress through discrete one-dimensional chains. Driven by conformational entropy, polymer chains inevitably coil in three-dimensional space, precluding effective stress transfer, thereby compromising the ultimate mechanical performance. Two-dimensional (2D) molecular sheets, with intrinsic in-plane rigidity, could in principle circumvent this constraint. Yet in existing assemblies, where stress transfers efficiently within each molecular sheet but poorly between them, their exceptional properties fail to translate to the macroscale. Here, we demonstrate a 2D highly oriented molecular network (2D HOMN), an ultra-stiff, super-tough polymeric material constructed by the solid-state covalent welding of assembled 2D polyaramid sheets with flexible linkers pre-grafted at their peripheries. Enabled by efficient intersheet load sharing and energy dissipation, the welded films rival the modulus and strength of Kevlar 29 fibers, reaching 69.8 and 3.9 GPa, with impact toughness up to an order of magnitude beyond Kevlar composites. This designed intersheet covalent connectivity further renders the 2D HOMN impermeable to gas molecules and ions, resilient to radiation and efficient in thermal transport. This work establishes 2D molecular motifs as heterogeneous monomeric building blocks and provides a general strategy for constructing multifunctional polymeric networks.

item.title: Curvilinear nanomagnets of non-trivial geometric topology
item.description: arXiv:2611.32306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this Chapter, we focus on the question of how the global geometric characteristics given by the topology of the sample's shape are reflected in the properties of the magnetization field of the given curvilinear nanoarchitecture. We start with a brief introduction to differential geometry and topology, giving their connection to the specific properties of the vector field represented by the magnetization field defined at the specific manifold. Then we discuss modern fabrication and characterization techniques that make analysis of a sample's topology not only an interesting theoretical concept but also a directly accessible and practically relevant topic. The main attention of the Chapter is dedicated to the theoretical and experimental analysis of nanostructrures with the topology different from the extended films beyond the in-depth studied topic of tubes of the constant radius. In particular, toroidal, spherical, and non-orientable manifolds are considered.

item.title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.32325v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resolving local atomic structures such as defects and interfaces from electron microscopy contrast relies heavily on researcher judgement, leading to low efficiency and subjective standards. Here we present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided and expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that turns one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable capabilities by updating executable operators, parameters and routing rules with versioned inheritance. Given researcher-defined tasks, the system selects analysis paths from image features without expert labels, while testing and inheriting code updates under fixed budgets. Combining physical priors with expert feedback improves atomic point-defect detection over larger models and raises cross-material interface coverage from 5.13% to 72.11% within a 10% area budget. Adapting the framework to micrographs from unseen studies further separates touching nanoparticles by aligning optimization with particle-level measurements. This work moves computational microscopy beyond standalone models and static scripts towards self-evolving platforms that accumulate human scientific expertise

item.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
item.description: arXiv:2611.32451v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Color defect centers carrying electron spins in solid crystals like diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for qubits and quantum sensors, with SiC material being particularly interesting due to its compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Here we investigated the electron spin properties of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) both electron spin $S = 3/2$ in 4H-SiC in the temperature range $T=80-300$~K using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The EPR spectrum shows central and satellite lines, where the former ones originate from V1 and V2 centers, as well as from unknown defect center X. The analysis of continuous wave EPR measurements revealed a spin concentration of $c_{\mathrm{V1}}=1.47\pm0.3\times10^{14}$, $c_{\mathrm{V2}}=5.6\pm1.12\times10^{13}$ and $c_{\mathrm{X}}=1.03\pm0.21\times10^{13}$ spins/cm$^{3}$. Additionally, electron spin coherence $T_2$ and relaxation times $T_1$ have been measured on the central and on the satellite spectral lines, resulting in longer $T_1$ and $T_2$ for the satellite transition, compared to the central one, with maximum values of $42.8\pm1.3$~ms and $0.708\pm0.004$~ms respectively at $T=80$~K. We reveal, that decoherence is mainly caused by nuclear and electron spin diffusion.

item.title: Reconfigurable Chiral Phonons and Their Selection in Asymmetrically Stacked Graphene MoirMoir\'{e} Superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.32466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral phonons, lattice vibrations carrying angular momentum, offer a new handle for controlling phonon-mediated phenomena in condensed matter, yet their on-demand generation and deterministic control remain challenging. Here we show, using helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy, that asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices provide a reconfigurable platform for chiral phonons. We observe a finite degree of circular polarization for both chiral interlayer shear phonons and intralayer optical phonons. A chiral-phonon Raman-tensor model attributes this response to interfacial $C_{2}$-symmetry breaking together with Raman resonance within the van Hove singularity region. Reversing either the twist sense or the stacking order inverts the degree of circular polarization through the spatial transformations linking the corresponding stacking geometries. By tuning the excitation energy and twist angle, we achieve nearly full-range control of the degree of circular polarization of interlayer shear phonons, from $-1$ to $1$, while gate-induced interlayer potential redistribution enables substantial and reversible in situ modulation. These results establish asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices as a versatile platform for generating and controlling chiral phonons, with implications for optoelectronic and quantum technologies.

item.title: Packing the Bragg sphere: complete three-dimensional photonic band gaps at the refractive index of polymers (1.55)
item.description: arXiv:2611.32789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Complete 3D photonic band gaps have so far been found only at refractive-index contrasts of about 1.9 and above, reached by rod-connected diamond lattice structures. Reciprocal-space design of quasiperiodic structures recently achieved considerable emission attenuation at much lower contrasts [L. Maiwald et al., Adv. Optical Mater. 10, 2100785 (2022)]. Here we implement systematic search and reciprocal-space design of periodic 3D structures with complete band gaps, solving a discrete optimization problem on an integer lattice. A gap above a high band needs the strongest Fourier components of the dielectric close to the Bragg sphere of that band. Crystals with large cells, started from Fourier peaks at the vertices of a polyhedron on this sphere and optimized against densely refined band edges, open complete gaps down to an index contrast of 1.55, that of common polymers against air. A rational approximant of an icosidodecahedron gave the most efficient location of the Fourier peaks among the polyhedra tested. Numerical calculations confirm the gaps over a resolution series, with band edges searched over the whole Brillouin zone. The best designs are connected porous networks, suited to a microwave test with printed polymer. A rigorous bound, valid for any structure, does not exclude gaps at lower index, and the next rational approximants of the icosidodecahedron, whose Bragg zones match bands 576 and 2440 almost exactly, point to where gaps at even lower contrast may be sought.

item.title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by $6r_S$, independently of the discretization order, where $r_S$ is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to $2^{26}$ points. For Rayleigh-B\'enard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.

item.title: A model colloidal gel former for the measurement of inter-particle forces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tracking of particle coordinates in colloidal model systems is an established technique. Recently, an emulsion system has been introduced where not only the coordinates, but also contacts and compressive forces between the droplets can be determined [Dong et al. J. Chem. Phys. 156 214907 (2022). Here we develop this system to control both the density mismatch and refractive index contrast between the emulsion droplets and the solvent. The former is important in minimizing sedimentation due to gravity and the latter is necessary for 3d imaging with confocal microscopy. By mapping our system carefully to computer simulation, we quantify interdroplet forces and packing geometries in depletion gels and probe the relationship between local structure and compressive stress. The simulations also provide ensemble measurements of the attractive part of the force between droplets and related quantities such as the stress tensor. Finally, we implement an improved measure of local stress in our experiments, which can be directly compared with the corresponding quantity in simulations. We find that locally rigid minimum energy clusters are associated with regions of higher stress in the gel network.

item.title: Robust growth of $\alpha$-tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using atomically thin titanium seed layer
item.description: arXiv:2611.33112v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tantalum (Ta) based superconducting circuits have attracted attention for their low microwave loss. However, reproducible growth of high-quality $\alpha$-phase Ta films remains challenging because film properties are highly sensitive to growth conditions. We present a robust, room-temperature route for $\alpha$-Ta growth on sapphire substrates using an ultrathin Ti seed layer, which significantly widens the accessible deposition parameter space. We compare this approach to Ta films grown at high temperature without a seed layer and at room temperature with a Nb seed. We assess films using structural and surface characterization and quantify microwave loss with coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonators measured in the quantum regime. We obtain two-level-system (TLS)-limited quality factors comparable to the state of the art for Ta-on-sapphire CPW resonators with similar geometries. In addition, temperature-dependent measurements reveal that high-temperature-grown films and films subjected to extended buffered-oxide etch treatment exhibit additional temperature activated loss, highlighting the role of growth route and post-processing in microwave performance. Our results establish ultrathin seed-layer engineering as a reliable alternative route to reproducible, low-loss $\alpha$-Ta films and motivate closer study of the interfacial mechanisms that govern Ta phase formation.

item.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.33155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].

item.title: Design of Chalcopyrite-Inspired Tellurides for Solar Cells: A First-Principles and Coupled FDTD-CHARGE Device Study
item.description: arXiv:2510.18078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The defect-chalcopyrite tellurides XGa$_2$Te$_4$ (X = Cd, Zn) are evaluated as photovoltaic absorbers by combining first-principles calculations with coupled optical and electrical device simulations. Density functional theory (PBEsol) yields tetragonal $I\bar{4}$ structures with negative formation energies and phonon spectra free of imaginary modes. Both compounds have direct band gaps at $\Gamma$ of 1.046 and 1.032 eV (PBEsol) and 2.21 and 1.895 eV (HSE06), with absorption coefficients above $10^5$ cm$^{-1}$ in the visible. Wannier-Mott estimates give exciton binding energies of 18.85 and 26.81 meV, comparable to $k_BT$ at 300 K, and Bohr radii of 3.43 and 2.30 nm. Constant-relaxation-time Boltzmann transport gives Seebeck coefficients up to ~255 $\mu$V K$^{-1}$ near 350-400 K. Mulliken-electronegativity estimates place both band edges outside the water redox potentials at pH 0, with hydrogen-evolution driving forces of 0.83 and 0.60 eV but oxygen-evolution margins of only 0.16 and 0.07 eV. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) optical simulations coupled to drift-diffusion (CHARGE) electrical simulations of FTO/IGZO/XGa$_2$Te$_4$/CuAlO$_2$/Pt cells reveal a small conduction-band spike at the front junction (+0.15 and +0.33 eV), reflection losses governed by interference in the front oxide stack, electron collection confined to ~0.5 $\mu$m from the junction, and a fill-factor loss in the CdGa$_2$Te$_4$ device caused by the CuAlO$_2$ hole contact. Because the imported optical constants retain the PBEsol absorption edge, the simulated photocurrents exceed the detailed-balance limit; absolute efficiencies are therefore treated as upper bounds, whereas the identified loss mechanisms and design trends are robust. These results identify CdGa$_2$Te$_4$ and ZnGa$_2$Te$_4$ as candidate thin-film absorbers and define the contact engineering required to exploit them.

item.title: Nanoindentation induced plasticity in equiatomic MoTaW alloys by experimentally guided machine learning molecular dynamics simulations
item.description: arXiv:2601.06846v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCA) exhibit exceptional strength and thermal stability, yet their plastic deformation mechanisms under complex contact loading remain insufficiently understood. Here, the nanoindentation response of an equiatomic MoTaW alloy is investigated through a combined experimental and atomistically resolved modeling approach. Spherical nanoindentation experiments are coupled with large scale molecular dynamics simulations employing a tabulated low dimensional Gaussian Approximation Potential (tabGAP), enabling near DFT accuracy. A physics based similarity criterion, implemented via PCA of load-displacement curves, is used to identify mechanically representative experimental responses for quantitative comparison with simulations. Indentation stress-strain curves are constructed yielding excellent agreement in the elastic regime between experiment and simulation, with reduced Young's moduli of approximately 270 GPa. Generalized stacking fault energy calculations reveal elevated unstable stacking- and twinning-fault energies in MoTaW relative to pure refractory elements, indicating suppressed localized shear and a preference for dislocation-mediated plasticity. Atomistic analyses demonstrate a strong crystallographic dependence of plastic deformation, with symmetric {110}<111> slip activation and four-fold rosette pile-ups for the [001] orientation, and anisotropic slip, strain localization, and enhanced junction formation for [011]. Local entropy and polyhedral template matching analyses further elucidate dislocation network evolution and deformation-induced local structural transformations. Overall, this study establishes a direct mechanistic link between fault energetics, orientation-dependent dislocation activity, and experimentally observed nanoindentation behavior in RCCA.

item.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
item.description: arXiv:2601.15735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. In the MAGNDATA database, 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. With the $k$ index fixed to its experimental value, about nine structures are generated per material on average. We perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. The characteristic energy scale among oriented SSA structures is only approximately 0.29 meV per magnetic atom, about 300 times smaller than that of distinct SSA structures. These results demonstrate that oriented SSG-based enumeration, combined with the two-step calculations for SSA and oriented SSA structures, provides an efficient and robust route for large-scale magnetic-structure prediction.
